solution:
The wrong pair is (3) Textiles Committee - welfare of weavers.

The Textile Committee was established according to the 'Textile Committee Act 1963', and its work is to set the quality standards for textiles manufactured for sale in the internal market as well as for export, not the welfare of weavers. The welfare of weavers is looked after by the 'Mega cluster' scheme, which helps weavers through self-finance groups and non-governmental organisations by giving raw material, design banks and development of technology.

The other three pairs are correct. The Industrial Finance Corporation of India was established in 1948 to make long term loans available to industrial projects, the Industrial Development Corporation was established in 1954 to bring about greater development of the industrial sector, and the Khadi and Village Industries Commission was established to give impetus to industrialisation in rural areas.

|  |  |
|---|---|
| Goods imported in India | Machines, iron, mineral oil, fertilisers, medicines. |
| Goods exported from India | Tea, coffee, spices, cotton textiles, leather, footwear, pearls, precious stones. The chapter also names jute products, vehicles, tractors and bicycles among the goods India exports. |

India's imports and exports together make up its foreign trade. When planning started in 1951, the import of industrial goods and of the raw material required for production increased. India's imports included machines, iron, mineral oil, fertilisers and medicines. After independence India also gave impetus to exports in order to gain valuable foreign exchange. India's exports included tea, coffee, spices, cotton textiles, leather, footwear, pearls and precious stones. Besides these, India is a major exporter of jute products, and vehicles, tractors and bicycles made in India are also sent to other countries.

Internal trade means the buying and selling of goods within the country. India's internal trade takes place via railways, waterways, roads and airways. Ports like Mumbai, Kolkata, Cochi and Chennai are important for this trade. Commodities like coal, cotton, cotton textiles, rice, wheat, raw jute, iron, steel, oilseeds, salt and sugar are included in internal trade. Goods made in one part of the country thus reach the people living in other parts.

The tourism industry has developed a lot in India because India has a rich cultural heritage. There are places of worship of different religions, pilgrimage centres, confluences of rivers, forts and caves all over the country, so there is something to visit in every region. Because of this variety, tourists from our own country as well as from abroad travel in India throughout the year and not only in one season. The facilities that tourists need for staying and travelling are provided through the Tourism Development Corporation, which makes travel easier. Along with this the hotel industry and the sale of curios thrive at tourist places, and guides are available to give tourists information about the area.

The quality of life and standard of living of Indian citizens is increasing because of the development of industries in the country. After independence institutions like the Industrial Finance Corporation of India and the Industrial Development Corporation were established to give loans to industrial projects and to develop the industrial sector, so many industries such as textile, silk, jute, automobile, cement, leather, salt and bicycle industries grew. When industries develop, many opportunities for employment become available and people earn a regular income. The Khadi and Village Industries Commission created such employment even in the villages and made them self-reliant, while agriculture, fisheries and tourism gave work to many more people. India is also rapidly becoming independent in food grain production. On the whole this progress of industry improves the standard of life in the country.

Agriculture is the major occupation in India and seventy percent of Indian society depends upon jobs related to agriculture, so the government makes many efforts to promote agricultural industries.

Loans are given to farmers through rural banks and cooperative institutions so that they can meet the cost of farming. Tools and implements, seeds and fertilisers are supplied to them. Study visits, agricultural outdoor trips and farmers' get-togethers are organised through the Panchayat Samitis to bring about improvements in agriculture. Farmers are given training regarding soil testing, nursery of fruit plants, pisciculture, poultry, cattle and goat rearing and dairy farming, and guidance is given to them by a district level training institute. Financial help is given to build warehouses for storing the farm produce, so that the crop is not wasted after the harvest. Modern techniques like drip irrigation and organic farming are used in farming. In the fourth five year plan the government placed focus on industries connected with farm produce, such as the food processing industry, the sugar industry and the motor-tractor industry. Because of all these efforts India is rapidly becoming independent in food grain production and in farming techniques.

India has a rich cultural heritage, and there are places of worship of different religions, pilgrimage centres, confluences of rivers, forts and caves all over the country. Tourists from our own country as well as from abroad travel in India throughout the year, and the needs of these tourists create employment for many people.

The facilities for tourists to stay and to travel are provided through the Tourism Development Corporation, and people get work in providing these facilities. The hotel industry thrives in tourist places, and so does the sale of curios, which gives work to those who make and sell them. In some places there are guides who give information to tourists about that area. Sometimes vehicles do not reach the destination in remote and difficult to reach tourist places, and there the local people help the tourists in return for a fee. Employment opportunities are generated out of all these needs of the tourists.

The government has reserved some forests for the industries that are based on forests, because these industries need forest produce as their raw material.

Forests supply the raw material for the construction industry, the paper industry and the newsprint industry. The silk industry is also based on forests, and research about the species of the silkworm and mulberry trees is done for it. The matchbox industry too needs forest raw material. Medicinal herbs, honey and lacquer are obtained from forests, and forests also give the raw material needed for paint.

Since all these industries depend on forests, the task of conservation of the forests is done by the central government, the State government and by the local people.

The leather industry is a big industry in India. It is primarily export oriented, which means that most of the goods it makes are sent to other countries rather than sold within India. Leather and footwear are named among the goods that India exports, and this trade helps the country to earn valuable foreign exchange. Leather goods were also one of the industries on which focus was placed in the fourth five year plan of the Central Government.

[Note: the chapter does not state where the leather industry is located in India, how much leather is produced, or the names of the countries to which leather goods are exported.]
